**Under the registered §3/§8 verdict lattice the result is "Partially-named": a rank-32 bilinear prefix×query interaction closes 93% of the additive-stitch → full-context R² gap on novel-prefix folds, but a small, significant unnamed nonlinear residual remains — and the same-protocol stitch-MLP on the disjoint [prefix; query] inputs (R² 0.920) exceeds the full-context linear map itself (0.914).**

- Levels: stitch PRESS-ridge 0.8491 → bilinear(r*=32) 0.9097 → stitch-MLP (3-seed ensemble) 0.9201; full-context ridge 0.9142. Interaction-gap fraction (bilinear−stitch)/(context−stitch) = 0.932; relative to the MLP-reachable ceiling it is 0.0606/0.0710 ≈ 85%.

This is fully consistent with Partially-named and rules out the stronger narration.
- Robustness across fold schemes: novel-query — Δ_named +0.0268 [0.0208, 0.0335] at r*=16, δ_beyond +0.0638 [0.0516, 0.0753] (the unnamed share is much LARGER under novel queries: bilinear 0.663 vs MLP 0.727); doubly-novel — Δ_named +0.0283 [0.0183, 0.0397] (two-way cluster CI over 921 prefix × 636 query groups, 2,900 rows), δ_beyond **unavailable** (no stitch-MLP was fit under the doubly scheme; stated as a coverage gap, not a null). ## Per-result reads

### 1. Fold hygiene (Gate A tripped): the banked n50k fitter comparison is contaminated; n1m is the citable context-arm gain

The banked #779 n50k split has 297 exact train↔target duplicates (154 affected targets) and 35,073 near-duplicate pairs at the round's own criterion (5-gram Jaccard ≥ 0.8), affecting **325 of 1,400** val/test targets — far over the 14-target (1%) Gate A threshold; the sensitivity bound is ≤ 0.325 of test R², i.e. unbounded for practical purposes. MinHash candidate recall at true J ≥ 0.8 was verified at 1.0 (876 planted pairs); the chunk reconstruction spot-check matched 500/500 prompts positionally. Gate A's letter called for the P0c dedup refit; the run recorded it infeasible at the realized chunk size and applied the plan §8 registered fallback instead: **the n50k gain is quoted UNAUDITED, and the n1m comparison is the citable context-arm nonlinearity gain.** The n1m re-verification is clean (0 exact, 0 near post-dedup; the banked round itself dropped 435 exact + 30,437 near): at L19, n_train = 963,444, ridge 0.754 [0.743, 0.764] → MLP w8192 0.810 — the ≈ +0.056 gap the Goal names. Scope caveat (registered): the audit criterion is LEXICAL only — semantic paraphrase duplicates are not screened, in n50k or n1m.

The #1092 fold re-derivation checks out exactly: 21,193 manifest rows → 19,708 trait-stratum-excluded → 17,308 battery-excluded fit rows; 996 prefix groups / 1,397 query groups, no group in more than one fold under either scheme.

### 2. Detection: dependence is everywhere the instrument can see it; the prefix-end read is fold-boundary-dependent

25 of the 30 registered tests (5 arms × 3 permutation schemes × {HSIC, dCor}, dense 99×48 core, B=1,000, Holm-corrected) reject at the permutation resolution floor (Holm p = 0.030). The planted-effect power check passed (context arm fired, as it must) with a measured minimal detectable effect ≈ 0.05 R²-equivalent — so any per-arm null here reads "no structure above MDE ≈ 0.05", never "the map is linear". The 5 non-rejections concentrate on context_end×query_block and three HSIC cells.

The prefix-end arm needs the registered fold-boundary adjudication: its input is constant within a prefix, so the within-prefix derangement (the only fold-clean scheme) is structurally uninformative for it — the permuted statistic is invariant (committed null q95 equals the observed value to 9 significant figures; the nominal dCor p=0.001 there is an artifact of a degenerate null). The only informative scheme, prefix-block, crosses fold boundaries, where per-fold map differences can register as dependence. Per-fold HSIC values are elevated in all 6 folds (3.0e-4 to 4.2e-4 vs the cross-fold null q95 3.2e-5) but no per-fold nulls were committed, so I adjudicate the prefix-end detection as **fold-boundary-dependent / not cleanly established** — the hypothesis that prefix-end residual dependence is "weak or absent" is neither confirmed nor refuted. Its mean-predictable part is in any case small (ladder gains +0.011–0.015).

Detection and estimation must be read together (registered): HSIC/dCor detect ANY dependence including heteroscedasticity, so firing tests are not gain claims.
